title: Short META — EU DSA Breach + AI Capex Margin Vise
entry: Short $595-612 on June 2 open or first session without a gap recovery above $625. Scale: 60% at open, add 40% on any intraday bounce to $615-620 that fails to hold 30 minutes. Do not initiate below $590 — wait for confirmation that the $600 level is resistance, not support.
stop_loss: $635 daily close (~5.4% above entry midpoint $602) — implies the EU DSA preliminary findings are resolved favorably (settlement disclosed before the formal Commission report) OR management provides explicit forward guidance that AI capex growth rate will decelerate materially starting Q3 2026, removing the margin-compression overhang
targets: $555 — initial capitulation low; confirmed EU DSA preliminary findings accelerate institutional de-rating; mirrors the first-leg decline in META's 2022 capex-overhang drawdown, -7.8%
$515 — Q2 2026 earnings preview period (late July): AI capex guidance of $125-145B translates to visible margin compression in Q2 cost structure; FCF re-rating downward by consensus, -14.5%
$470 — full regulatory overhang priced: EU structural remedy plus AI capex retracement from guidance peak; similar to Meta's September 2022 trough, -22.0%
catalyst: Two converging forces broke META on June 2: (1) EU Digital Services Act preliminary breach findings from the European Commission, carrying potential fines and operational restrictions on Meta's algorithmic recommendation engine — historically the highest-margin component of its ad stack; (2) a $125-145B AI capex guidance range for FY2026, a figure approximately 2.5x FY2024 actual spend, triggering analyst models to revise FCF forecasts downward even while assuming the capex eventually converts to revenue. The combination of a regulatory ceiling on the highest-margin revenue stream and a capex floor compressing free cash flow creates a classic margin-compression vise.
thesis:
META's stock declined 4-5% on June 2 not because the underlying business is deteriorating but because two independent valuation ceilings appeared simultaneously. The EU DSA preliminary breach findings represent the more immediate catalyst: the Commission's preliminary view is that Meta's algorithmic recommendation systems on Facebook and Instagram violate DSA Article 27 (risk mitigation obligations for very large online platforms). If sustained in the formal determination, the remedy could require Meta to offer users a chronological-only feed option — eliminating the algorithmic personalization layer that generates approximately 30-40% of its ad CPM premium relative to competitors. The fine itself (up to 6% of global annual revenue, approximately $7B) is secondary to the operational restriction risk, which markets have not yet fully priced.

The AI capex overhang is the slower-moving but equally important pressure. Management's $125-145B FY2026 AI capex guidance is the single largest capital allocation in Meta's history, implying a step-function increase in the depreciation and amortization load that will constrain reported FCF for 3-4 years before the AI advertising-targeting and virtual-reality monetization cycles mature. Investors who bought META at $580-640 over the prior quarter were pricing a benign capex trajectory; the updated guidance requires a valuation reset at any multiple above 22x forward EBITDA.

The entry is explicitly near the current level ($600 after the 4-5% intraday decline). The thesis rests on neither catalyst being resolved quickly: the EU DSA formal determination process takes months from preliminary findings to final decision, maintaining a regulatory overhang through the summer earnings period; and AI capex will not resolve until at least Q2 2026 earnings (late July), when investors can assess whether the spending rate is front-loaded or sustained at the $145B annual rate. During this 4-6 week window, META has no positive re-rating catalyst.

The counter-party is the long-term META bull who argues — correctly on a multi-year view — that Meta's AI advertising stack (Advantage+ campaign automation, AI Overviews-adjacent placement, and Llama-powered content recommendation) is generating demonstrable advertiser ROI and will eventually justify the capex. That thesis is not wrong over a 2-3 year horizon. But the risk is asymmetric over the next 4 weeks: regulatory uncertainty is a month-old negative just entering the institutional news cycle; capex compression is a Q2 report-month concern; and the macro STEP ASIDE regime means any negative incremental data gets amplified in a market searching for reasons to reduce risk.
bull_case: EU Commission releases a favorable preliminary settlement outline before the formal DSA decision — META gaps back above $635 on relief. Simultaneously, management communicates at an investor conference that AI capex front-loading will plateau in Q3, with FCF recovery visible by Q4 2026. Stock recovers to $650+. Short stopped out at $635.
bear_case: EU Commission preliminary findings become a formal Article 66 determination; simultaneous US FTC Instagram divestiture case advances to trial in H2 2026, creating a compound regulatory discount. AI capex guidance is raised at Q2 earnings (late July) from $145B to $160B+. META revisits the $470-490 range within the 2-4 week horizon in an accelerated bear scenario.
invalidation: Daily close above $635, OR management provides clear forward guidance that AI capex growth decelerates materially starting Q3 2026, OR EU DSA preliminary findings are formally resolved with a settlement below $3B and no operational restrictions on the recommendation engine
